source.text: ተአመኑ፡ ጻድቃን፡ እስመ፡ ለጽእለት፡ ይከውኑ፡ ኃጥአን፡ ወይትሐጐሉ፡ በዕለተ፡ ዓመፃ።
source.note: Whole selected-critical corrective proposal against Charles1906 printed201/PDF239, using original Uoft camera pixels and same-edition Claremont comparison. The main-line Alf spelling in the reproach noun is retained, not normalized to the lexicon head. LOW qualifies this bounded orthographic/lexical inference and reported apparatus variation; it is not an unreadable-letter placeholder or new manuscript certification. Explicit withdrawn root misreadings remain immutable in research history.
transcription_uncertainties: No unread main-line letter is asserted in this revised proposal. Selected W4AlfVI versus lexical Ain-family spelling requires the bounded explanation and exact peer assessment; different roots are not conflated.

translation.text: Be confident, righteous ones, for sinners will become an object of reproach[a] and perish on the day of injustice.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected text spells the reproach noun with Alf, while the corresponding lexicon head is spelled with Ain. This translation identifies the forms as orthographic variants, retaining the printed source spelling. The noun conveys reproach or disgrace; the verb means be or become, not die. This is a bounded lexical identification, not a claim that the spelling is uniform across manuscripts.

This follows Charles1906’s selected edited text, not a newly collated manuscript. His apparatus26 reports that u omits the next ten words, and27 reports an omission by t at the conjunction before the perishing verb. These are his reports, not independent manuscript checks; the ten-word omission is not equated with this nine-word verse. The final phrase is literally on the day of injustice, without an added date or named agent of destruction.
